item.title: New public spending watchdog set to be appointed next year
item.description: A PROPOSITION to appoint Paul Dossett as Jersey’s next Comptroller and Auditor General has been lodged by the Chief Minister. The seven-year fixed term of the current Comptroller and Auditor General Lynn Pamment CBE is due to end on 31 December 2026. If approved by the States Assembly, Mr Dossett will take up the post […] The post New public spending watchdog set to be appointed next year appeared first on Jersey Evening Post.

item.title: Social rented housing eligibility changes come into force
item.description: MORE Islanders are now able to apply for social rented housing, as changes to eligibility criteria come into force yesterday. The new rules, introduced by Housing Minister Sam Mézec, lower the minimum age for applicants without children from 25 to 18 year olds. item.title: Philip Ozouf avoids jail over immigration offences
item.description: ONE of Jersey’s most recognisable politicians was this morning sentenced to 120 hours of community service for immigration offences. St Saviour Deputy Philip Ozouf appeared in the Royal Court after admitting a string of charges relating to the employment of Rwandan nationals. item.title: Shared housing in Jersey and the gradual transition to independence
item.description: By Bernard Place FOR many young Islanders, the first step out of the family home has become increasingly difficult. item.description: THOUSANDS of responses to a public consultation on the proposed 2030 phase-out of petrol and diesel vehicles are now being analysed.
